31941-rationalism.title: Rationalism
31941-rationalism.creator: Unknown
31941-rationalism.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The names 'rationalist' and 'rationalism' have been used in so many senses within the past three hundred years that they cannot be said to stand quite definitely for any type or school of philosophic thought.

arxiv-2104-05781.title: Censored Semi-Bandits for Resource Allocation
arxiv-2104-05781.creator: Arun Verma, Manjesh K. Hanawal, Arun Rajkumar, Raman Sankaran
arxiv-2104-05781.description: Abstract We consider the problem of sequentially allocating resources in a censored semi-bandits setup, where the learner allocates resources at each step to the arms and observes loss. The loss depends on two hidden parameters, one specific to the arm but independent of the resource allocation, and the other depends on the allocated resource.

arxiv-2109-09843.title: System Size and Flavour Dependence of Chemical Freeze-out Temperatures in ALICE Data from pp, pPb and PbPb Collisions at LHC Energies
arxiv-2109-09843.creator: Fernando Antonio Flor, Gabrielle Olinger, René Bellwied
arxiv-2109-09843.description: Abstract We present the system size and flavour dependence of the chemical freeze-out temperature ( T ch T_{\mathrm{ch}} ) at vanishing baryo-chemical potential calculated via thermal fits to experimental yields for several multiplicity classes in pp, pPb and PbPb collisions measured by ALICE.

arxiv-2206-07900.title: Quest for eternal oscillons
arxiv-2206-07900.creator: T. S. Mendonça, H. P. de Oliveira
arxiv-2206-07900.description: Abstract Nonlinear field theories produce unstable but long-lived configurations known as oscillons. These structures have been studied with asymmetric and symmetric double-well potentials and extended to other forms of potentials. In the present work, we examine the consequences of considering higher-order field theories, where we have used a generalization of the symmetric double-well potential and a ϕ 6 \phi^{6} potential.

arxiv-2210-02263.title: High average gradient in a laser-gated multistage plasma wakefield accelerator
arxiv-2210-02263.creator: A. Knetsch, I.A. Andriyash, M. Gilljohann, O. Kononenko, A. Matheron, Y. Mankovska, P. San Miguel Claveria, V. Zakharova, E. Adli, S. Corde
arxiv-2210-02263.description: Abstract Plasma wakefield accelerators driven by particle beams are capable of providing accelerating gradient several orders of magnitude higher than currently used radio-frequency technology, which could reduce the length of particle accelerators, with drastic influence on the development of future colliders at TeV energies and the minimization of x-ray free-electron lasers.

arxiv-2402-06497.title: Iris-SAM: Iris Segmentation Using a Foundation Model
arxiv-2402-06497.creator: Parisa Farmanifard, Arun Ross
arxiv-2402-06497.description: Abstract Iris segmentation is a critical component of an iris biometric system and it involves extracting the annular iris region from an ocular image. In this work, we develop a pixel-level iris segmentation model from a foundation model, viz., Segment Anything Model (SAM), that has been successfully used for segmenting arbitrary objects.

arxiv-2406-18924.title: Learning Pareto Set for Multi-Objective Continuous Robot Control
arxiv-2406-18924.creator: Tianye Shu, Ke Shang, Cheng Gong, Yang Nan, Hisao Ishibuchi
arxiv-2406-18924.description: Abstract For a control problem with multiple conflicting objectives, there exists a set of Pareto-optimal policies called the Pareto set instead of a single optimal policy. When a multi-objective control problem is continuous and complex, traditional multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) algorithms search for many Pareto-optimal deep policies to approximate the Pareto set, which is quite resource-consuming.

arxiv-2509-09397.title: Decoupling Clinical and Class-Agnostic Features for Reliable Few-Shot Adaptation under Shift
arxiv-2509-09397.creator: Umaima Rahman and Raza Imam and Mohammad Yaqub and Dwarikanath Mahapatra
arxiv-2509-09397.description: Abstract Medical vision-language models (VLMs) offer promise for clinical decision support, yet their reliability under distribution shifts remains a major concern for safe deployment. These models often learn task-agnostic correlations due to variability in imaging protocols and free-text reports, limiting their generalizability and increasing the risk of failure in real-world settings.

pmc-10595247.title: Establishment of a social listening mechanism on refugee crisis
pmc-10595247.creator: A Timotin, V Mita, A Paladi, V Chihai, O Lozan
pmc-10595247.description: BackgroundThe Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 captured the public attention. For the Republic of Moldova, a border country that sheltered the highest number of refugees reported to its local population, managing the refugee crisis became a challenge, including countering mis- and disinformation with major impact on public health.

pmc-11475812.title: Genomic and Socioeconomic Determinants of Racial Disparities in Breast Cancer Survival: Insights from the All of Us Program
pmc-11475812.creator: Nubaira Rizvi, Hui Lyu, Leah Vaidya, Xiao-Cheng Wu, Lucio Miele, Qingzhao Yu, Farrukh Aqil
pmc-11475812.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryResearch shows that Black women generally have poorer breast cancer survival rates than White women in the U.S. Our study aims to identify genomic variants and socioeconomic determinants that might explain this racial disparity using mediation analysis. Based on the All of US research program, we identified 15 gene mutations along with factors age, general health, and general quality of life that can explain the observed racial disparity.

pmc-11960282.title: The effect of a structured running exercise intervention on non-exercise physical activity and sedentary behaviour in persons with mild Multiple Sclerosis and healthy controls
pmc-11960282.creator: Ine Nieste, Jan Spaas, Wouter M A Franssen, Paul V Asch, Hans H C M Savelberg, Bert O Eijnde
pmc-11960282.description: BackgroundExercise interventions fail to increase objective physical activity (PA) in persons with Multiple Sclerosis (PwMS), while they self-report higher exercise participation. This suggests that PwMS change their non-exercise PA (NEPA). We aimed to explore NEPA changes of PwMS and healthy controls (HC), and whether these constrain exercise adaptations.MethodsTwenty-nine mildly-disabled PwMS and 26 HC completed a 10-month home-based running program.

pmc-12470823.title: Untargeted Plasma Metabolomics Extends the Biomarker Profile of Mitochondrial Neurogastrointestinal Encephalomyopathy
pmc-12470823.creator: Bridget E Bax, Sema Kalkan Uçar, Esther Imperlini
pmc-12470823.description: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE) is caused by pathogenic mutations in the nuclear TYMP gene, which encodes the cytosolic enzyme thymidine phosphorylase. In addition to the systemic accumulation of thymidine and deoxyuridine, several case studies have reported abnormalities in a range of other metabolites in patients with MNGIE.

pmc-12650737.title: Swimming Behavior of Percocypris pingi in the Wake of D-Shaped Obstacles: A Comparative Study of Single- and Dual-Fish Swimming in Complex Hydrodynamic Environments
pmc-12650737.creator: Lijian Ouyang, Qihao Meng, Qin Zhao, Liang Yu, Yike Li, Zebin Zhang, Li Tian, Zhiyuan Yang, Jiabin Lu, Weiwei Yao
pmc-12650737.description: The changes in water flow caused by hydropower projects and river diversions have had a profound impact on aquatic ecosystems, especially due to artificial structures such as dams and bridge piers. This study investigates the swimming behavior differences between single and dual fish in the wake region behind a D-shaped obstacle, using Percocypris pingi as the experimental species.

pmc-12751513.title: Risk factors for postoperative venous thromboembolism in patients with ovarian cancer
pmc-12751513.creator: Shi-Rui Jia, Chao-Hong Deng, Aziguli Yimamu, Jing Liu
pmc-12751513.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPostoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common and life-threatening complication in ovarian cancer surgery, which not only prolongs the patient’s hospital stay but also increases the risk of postoperative death. Based on this, this study aims to explore the factors affecting the incidence of postoperative VTE in ovarian cancer patients, so as to provide a reference for clinical risk assessment and targeted prophylactic measures.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted involving 67 patients with ovarian cancer who developed postoperative VTE at our hospital.

pmc-13062403.title: Functional and Radiological Outcome of Capitellum Fracture Fixation with Headless Screws Through Lateral Approach To Elbow, a Prospective Observational Study
pmc-13062403.creator: Udit Sourav Sahoo, Prajnadipta Rout, Kartik Chandra Pati
pmc-13062403.description: Introduction:Capitellum fractures are rare injuries contributing only 1% of all elbow fractures. Being such a rare injury, there is a lack of consensus with regard to the treatment recommendations. This study aims to evaluate the functional outcome of capitellum fractures treated by open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with headless screws through a lateral approach.

pmc-13451034.title: Indoor Air Nicotine, Nitrogen Dioxide Exposure, and COVID-19 Outcomes in a Great Plains Tribal Community
pmc-13451034.creator: Anna Tillery, Rae O’Leary, Nora Pisanic, Brittany Youpee, Angela Aherrera, Kate Krucynski, Jaylynn Farlee, Megan Wilks, Erena S. Hovhannisyan Romero, Miranda Cajero, Jacob Duran, Christopher Heaney, Ana M. Rule, Esther Erdei
pmc-13451034.description: Introduction:Indigenous communities in the United States have disproportionately high tobacco use and reliance on propane for heating and cooking fuel compared to other demographic groups. Of concern is exposure to air nicotine (AN) and NO2 in indoor environments and their potential impact on respiratory infections.

pmc-13499269.title: The second unprovoked seizure in a cohort of treated patients with a first unprovoked seizure
pmc-13499269.creator: Revital Gandelman‐Marton, Jacques Theitler
pmc-13499269.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesTo evaluate the rate of a second unprovoked seizure in antiseizure medications (ASMs)‐treated patients following a first unprovoked seizure and to identify potential risk factors associated with its occurrence.MethodsA retrospective review of the computerized database and the medical records of all the patients who presented to our outpatient epilepsy clinic following admission and ASM initiation due to a first unprovoked seizure during a decade (2012–2021).ResultsThe study group included 60 patients aged 18–84 years (mean: 40.8 years), 35 (58.3%) men.

pmc-13611072.title: Image-Based Identification of Ophthalmic Lens Optical Characteristics: A Benchmark of Local Texture Descriptors for Non-Destructive Optical Inspection
pmc-13611072.creator: Abdelilah Errachidi, Issam El Khadiri, Youssef El Merabet, Mohamed Kas, Yassine Ruichek, Cyril Meurie, Zahid Akhtar
pmc-13611072.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite recent advances in computer vision and optical imaging, the image-based recognition of ophthalmic lens categories characterized by different refractive indices and anti-reflective coating types remains largely unexplored. In this work, we formulate this problem as a non-destructive optical inspection task, where lens-induced visual changes are treated as subtle micro-texture signatures produced by the interaction between the lens and a controlled visual target. Although these signatures are often imperceptible to the human eye, they can be quantified using local texture analysis.
